authors: Z. Bern, J.J.M. Carrasco, H. Johansson, R. Roiban
title: The five-loop four-point amplitude of N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory
claim: The complete (full-colour) five-loop four-point N=4 SYM integrand (416 cubic graphs) is constructed with the method of maximal cuts; its UV divergence in the critical dimension D_c=26/5 is computed: for SU(Nc) it is single-trace with leading-colour and 1/Nc^2-suppressed pieces only, no double-trace terms, expressed via three positive vacuum integrals (subleading/leading ratio 45.0/Nc^2).
loop_order: 5 loops (full colour); UV pole in D=26/5
theory: N=4 SYM continued to D dims (16-supercharge SYM)
scheme: DR with eps=(26/5-D)/2; small-external-momentum expansion to about 185 vacuum diagrams reduced by consistency relations (eq. 4); vacuum integrals evaluated numerically (FIESTA).
symmetry_argument: Maximal-cut method in D dims (cuts evaluated in D dims via auxiliary cuts); finiteness bound D < 4 + 6/L cited (eq. 1); no regulated-action SUSY argument.

proved: Integrand matches maximal and next-to-maximal cuts down to k=3 (410, 2473, 7917, 15156 nonvanishing cuts for k=0..3).
UV pole in D=26/5 computed numerically (eq. 5).
assumed: D-dimensional cut agreement not separately verified numerically like the 4d supersum checks; completeness of cuts below k=3 not shown on page.
Supergravity sharing the same critical dimension is a conjecture.
checked_partially: Numerical evaluation of vacuum integrals; cut checks numerical in 4d.

evidence: Eqs. (2)-(3): 416 cubic graphs, generalized gauge freedom of numerators.
Eq. (4): vacuum expansion and reduction; eq. (5): divergence in terms of V(a), V(b), V(c).
red_flags: UV coefficient in non-integer D=26/5 depends on the D-dimensional completeness of the integrand, which is checked on cuts but not derived from a D-dimensional regulated SUSY action.
cross_checks: Planar part consistent with S1d.03_BCJK2007; integrand reused in N=8 five-loop analysis S1d.07_BCCJPRZ2018.
notes: This is the correct paper for the brief's '5-loop UV in D=26/5' lead.
